title: A generically finite morphism over a finite generic fibre is finite over a dense open of the target

standard_prerequisites.name: The generic finiteness statement producing a dense open of the target and an open of the source over which the restriction is finite, cited from the same chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Provides the pair of opens in the separated case, which then has to be proved to exhaust the preimage.

standard_prerequisites.name: A finite morphism is closed and proper, and the image of a proper scheme over the target is closed
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows that the open piece is also closed inside the preimage of the chosen open, which forces the complementary open to be empty.

standard_prerequisites.name: A quasi-compact scheme contains a dense open separated subscheme, and for a quasi-compact morphism whose image of a closed subset misses a point there is an open neighbourhood of that point whose preimage misses that subset, both cited from the properties chapter and the same chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces the quasi-compact case to the separated case by first restricting to a separated dense open of the source.

core_obligations: Reduce to an irreducible affine target: since the target has finitely many irreducible components one may pass to a dense open which is a disjoint union of them, and then the fibre over the generic point is finite because there are finitely many generic points upstairs (proof lines 13341-13344).

Separated case: take the dense open pair given by the generic finiteness statement, use that the restriction is finite hence closed and proper to see that the source open is closed as well as open in the preimage of the target open, and conclude that the complementary open piece is empty because the open piece contains all generic points of the source (proof lines 13345-13353).

Quasi-compact case: the source is quasi-compact, hence contains a dense open separated subscheme which contains all generic points, so the generic point of the target is not in the image of its complement; by quasi-compactness of that complement there is an open neighbourhood of the generic point whose preimage lies inside the separated open, and restricting there reduces to the separated case (proof lines 13355-13367).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to an irreducible affine target with finite generic fibre (proof lines 13341-13344).

Apply generic finiteness and use closedness of finite morphisms to reach the separated case, then reduce the quasi-compact case to it by first making the source separated over a dense open (proof lines 13345-13367).
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that a locally finite type morphism whose generic fibres match up, in the sense that the preimages of the generic points of the target are exactly the generic points of the source, with finitely many such points, is finite over a dense open of the target, provided the morphism is quasi-compact or separated (statement lines 13328-13339). The counted proof is a two-case argument: after reducing to an irreducible affine target it applies generic finiteness and uses closedness of finite morphisms to show the open piece already exhausts the preimage in the separated case, and in the quasi-compact case it first restricts to a dense open separated subscheme of the source and then reduces to the separated case by pushing the complement away from the generic point (proof lines 13341-13367). It is H2: both cases are carried out in the counted span, with the cited inputs being generic finiteness, closedness of finite morphisms and the existence of dense separated opens.
